open_points.subject: A5 token-file decoding
open_points.text: The file is decoded in that encoding, a byte sequence it cannot decode ending the start
open_points.question: Does any decoding error end startup, and what startup outcome or exit status must it produce?
options: Any decoding error refuses startup with START_FAILED.
A decoding error follows the implementation's codec or startup-exception behaviour.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup with START_FAILED on any decoding error.

witness.initial: The credential file contains a byte sequence that is invalid in TOKEN_ENCODING.
events: The service reads and attempts to decode the credential file.
outcomes: The codec exception or implementation-specific error handling determines whether and how startup ends.

open_points.subject: A5 accepted token form
open_points.text: the 32 random bytes in URL-safe Base64, 43 characters of `A`-`Z`, `a`-`z`, `0`-`9`, `-` and `_`
open_points.question: Must a loaded token have exactly the generated 43-character URL-safe Base64 form, or is every trimmed token of at least TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH characters from TOKEN_ALPHABET accepted?
options: Accept any token meeting TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH and TOKEN_ALPHABET.
Require the exact form only for generated tokens, not externally supplied credential files.
open_points.default_guess: Require the exact form only when generating a token; accept loaded tokens according to TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH and TOKEN_ALPHABET.

witness.initial: The credential file contains 32 exclamation marks, has safe permissions and is otherwise valid.
events: A caller sends those characters as the Bearer token.
outcomes: The service starts and authenticates the caller because the token meets TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH and TOKEN_ALPHABET.
The service refuses to start because the token is not the specified 43-character URL-safe Base64 form.

open_points.subject: A8 INTAKE_ID_SEPARATOR
open_points.question: Which construction must read INTAKE_ID_SEPARATOR, and at exactly which boundaries of `deliverer-photo-<project_id>-<source_id>` is it inserted?
options: Insert it after INTAKE_ID_PREFIX as well, producing an additional separator because the prefix already ends in `-`.
Keep the literal M05 construction and do not read this constant.

open_points.subject: A8 service exit classification
open_points.text: `ServiceExit` is SERVED, value `served`, a stop by a signal after the service has served, and START_FAILED, value `start_failed`, a start that fails before listening.
open_points.question: What outcome applies after listening but before the first request has been served, to a clean shutdown not caused by a signal, and to a runtime failure after listening?
options: Listening completes startup, so every subsequent orderly or signal-driven stop is SERVED; runtime failures have a separately specified process outcome.
SERVED requires at least one completed request; an earlier stop is START_FAILED.
Add separate outcomes for stopping before the first request, clean non-signal shutdown and runtime failure.
open_points.default_guess: Treat successful listening as the boundary: a later orderly or signal-driven stop is SERVED, while runtime failures use an explicitly specified nonzero status.

witness.initial: The service has begun listening but has not handled a request.
events: The process receives a termination signal.
outcomes: It selects SERVED and exits with status 0.
It cannot select SERVED because it has served no request, while START_FAILED also does not apply because it is already listening.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Which time source supplies marked_at, in what representation and time zone it is stored, at what point in the mark operation it is read, and how many readings a mark operation takes?
options: Read an injected clock exactly once when creating the mark and store naive UTC.
Read an injected clock exactly once when creating the mark and store offset-aware UTC.
Use ambient system time, with representation chosen by the implementation.
open_points.default_guess: Read an injected clock exactly once after validation and before writing the new mark, and store naive UTC consistently with the product's other delivered datetimes.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a mark; the service runs in Europe/Madrid when local time differs from UTC.
events: The calling flow records the Portal photo id.
The service creates and persists the publication mark.
A later operation reads the mark.
outcomes: marked_at is a naive UTC value from one injected-clock reading.
marked_at is local time, offset-aware UTC, or a value read at a different stage from an ambient clock.
witness.observer: The calling flow, a record reader or a generated-service test
